_note: FURNISHING PASS on top of the shell pass. Build scripts live in scratchpad/off8/ (o8kit.py = shared facts + wall-skin helper, o8_openings.py = the real cut openings, o8_shell.py = ceiling/trim/wainscot/windows/doors, o8_floor.py = the plank tone field, o8_desks.py, o8_stuff.py). Every script is idempotent by piece name, so re-running rebuilds and re-places without duplicating. 'Office Ceiling', 'Office Baseboards', 'Office Floor' and 'Office Wall Wash' match objects.js SURFACE_RE so they stay pickable:false; every furniture name deliberately avoids it. Verified with roomkit.check_pick 8 --level 1.
_orientation_derivation: Room 8 world x 28.8..39.4, z -4.5..7.1 -> local x 0(W)..10.6(E), z 0(N)..11.6(S). Adjacencies from roomkit.rooms --list: room 23 Bathroom x 18.7..28.6 z -4.3..3.1 is WEST (covering local z 0..7.6); room 22 Office printers x 33.2..39.4 z 7.1..12.9 is SOUTH-EAST; room 9 Laundry x 21.9..32.9 z 7.3..13.0 is SOUTH-WEST; nothing exists at x>39.4 or z<-4.5, so NORTH and EAST are EXTERIOR. Cross-checked against docs/floor plan/Main Floor Plan App.png, which is rotated 180 from world (world +x -> image left, world +z -> image up; Frontyard z=35..43 is at the top of the plan and the backyard z=-22.5 at the bottom). At 22.6 px/ft the plan puts the office in the building's corner and draws TWO pale-blue window ticks on its left-hand (= world EAST) exterior edge, at local z 0.2-3.4 and 8.0-11.0, and no wall between local x 6 and the east wall on its upper (= world SOUTH) edge -- the cased opening to the printer nook. The DB already carried one opening, edge 3 (WEST) offset 1.01 width 3.0, i.e. local z 7.59-10.59: the 15-lite french door. Photo B confirms the wall order left-to-right (= clockwise from the camera in the NE corner): east desk, SOUTH wall with the nook opening, WEST wall with the french door, north-west with the L desk.

_surfaces._note: The room-level colours are unchanged; the visible surfaces are now GLB: 'Office Floor' (grey LVP planks, N-S, 0.58 ft wide) over the slab and 'Office Wall Wash' (per-wall non-emissive albedo skins) over the paint.

_openings.note: 15-lite french door -- the room's only door
cased opening into the printer nook, room 22

_camera.why: Walls are FrontSide with inward normals so the two nearest the camera are culled. doll_sw culls SOUTH and WEST; this room's content -- the framed print and the L desk on the north wall, both windows and the east workstation -- lives on NORTH and EAST, which stay standing. The west wall carries only the door (a real cut, so nothing floats when it is culled) and the south wall's cabinet/clock are occluded by the printer nook's own north wall from that angle anyway.

_metered._method: roomkit.shot --day, then scratchpad/lr5/m.py with an overlay of every sample box (shots/*_boxes.png). Photo values are from Office A.jpg, the primary reference; photo f is a brighter exposure (its floor meters 174 against A's 110) and was used only for geometry.

walls_above_rail_render._samples: n=37400 / 30000 px clean patches in the look_n/e/w/s poses, north sampled off-centre to miss the print

Office Ceiling.what: one-sided downward plane (own dimmer emissive: kit.CEIL rendered 208 against the photo's 181), three-step crown, five cans, supply register, smoke detector

Office Baseboards.what: skirting + charcoal wainscot + two-step chair rail at 3.30 ft on all four walls, gapped at every real opening; both east window units (casing, stool, apron, jamb returns, white 2in venetian blinds, daylight pane); the 15-lite french door leaf and casing; the nook's cased opening; five white outlet plates on the charcoal and a switch plate by the door

Office Wall Wash.what: per-wall NON-emissive albedo skins, rail to crown, corner to corner, holes at every opening, roughness 0.95 to match the room wall. n #86807a / e #f4f2ed / s #fbfaf6 / w #bfbdb6, solved from two-point log-linear fits measured off real renders

Office Floor.what: grey LVP plank tone field: 0.58 ft planks running north-south with staggered butt joints, 7 shared tones + a dark seam plane

Office Desks.what: the L desk wrapping the NW corner (north leg 0.3-6.35, west return to z 7.05, rounded inner corner) with the curved 34in ultrawide, keyboard/mouse on a black mat, headphone stand, white globe lamp, succulent, figures, a white 3-drawer pedestal, a tower on the floor, and a light-grey mesh task chair

Office Workstation East.what: the sit/stand desk down the east wall under the windows: cream desk pad, wooden monitor riser, 27in monitor with webcam, white keyboard and mouse, two white pedestals, book stack, pen pots, figures, and a grey mesh chair with the green throw over its back

Office Art North.what: the framed specimen-grid print, 2.5 x 2.7 ft, bottom rail 4.35 ft AFF, light oak frame and wide white mat

Office Cabinet White.what: the white beadboard two-door cabinet on the south wall with the leaf-print tote on top

Office Plant Fig.what: fiddle-leaf fig, black ribbed planter on a black metal stand, white pebble dressing, two curved stems -- SE corner in front of the south window

Office Clutter.what: four floor totes, a stack of binders, the tall clear-liner bin, the black round bin, the small bin under the east desk, the bladeless fan, and the south wall's round clock + black wall tablet

_gaps: The SOUTH wall is capped at 165.8 even with a pure-white skin -- it is the wall the sun never reaches and no albedo can lift it further. All four walls now sit within 23 bytes (was 85) but the south is still ~20 below the other three.

In the doll_sw quadrant the printer nook's own north wall occludes the office's southern strip, so the cabinet, the clock/tablet and most of the floor totes are only visible from inside the room, never from the dollhouse.

Photo A (the primary reference, and what the tone is matched to) shows LIGHT GREY mesh chairs; the newer photo f shows a black Razer gaming chair at the L desk and a black mesh chair at the east desk. Built to photo A.
The north wall renders flat at 188.7 because it carries a single albedo skin; the photo has a real 167->205 gradient across it from the east windows. The mean matches, the gradient does not.
Photo A's desk surfaces are far more crowded than this (cosmetics, cables, papers, a hair dryer, a walking pad on the floor). Density is up a lot but still below the photo.
The passage is cut in room 8's south wall only; room 22's own north wall is still solid, so from outside you look through the office's hole at the nook's wall.
